title: Chapter 3 (Part 2): To Whom Morality Applies, Moral Responsibility and Why Be Moral
content:
🎓 ሰላም የEthioFresh ጀግኖች! 👋 የሞራልና ዜግነት ትምህርት ምዕራፍ ሶስት ክፍል ሁለት እንኳን ደህና መጣችሁ! ዛሬ ሞራል ለማን ወይም ለምን ነገር ይሠራል፣ ማን ሞራላዊ ተጠያቂ ነው፣ ድርጊት ሞራላዊ የሚያደርገው ምንድን ነው እና ሰው ለምን ሞራላዊ መሆን አለበት የሚለውን እንመለከታለን። ቡናችሁን ይዛችሁ በትኩረት አንብቡ! ☕📘

Chapter Three (Part 2): To Whom Morality Applies, Moral Responsibility and Why We Should Be Moral

3.4. To Whom or What Does Morality Apply?

In discussing the application of morality, four aspects may be considered: religious morality, morality and nature, individual morality, and social morality. Each aspects answers a different question: to whom, or to what, our moral obligations are owed. Religious morality concerns the human relationship with a supernatural being; morality and nature concerns the human relationship with the natural world; individual morality concerns a person’s relationship with their own conscience; and social morality concerns the relationship between human beings themselves.

👉 ሞራል ማንን ወይም ምንን ይመለከታል? ብለን ስንጠይቅ አራት ገጽታዎችን እናገኛለን። ሃይማኖታዊ ሞራል ከእግዚአብሔር ወይም ከአምላክ ጋር ያለን ግንኙነት፣ ሞራልና ተፈጥሮ ከተፈጥሮ ጋር ያለን ግንኙነት፣ ግላዊ ሞራል ከራሳችን ህሊና ጋር ያለን ግንኙነት፣ እና ማህበራዊ ሞራል ሰዎች እርስ በርሳቸው ያላቸውን ግንኙነት ይመለከታሉ። 🧭

3.4.1. Religious Morality

Religious morality refers to a human being in relationship to a supernatural being or beings. In the Jewish and Christian traditions, for example, the first three of the Ten Commandments pertain to this kind of morality. These commandments deal with a person’s relationship with God, not with any other human beings. By violating any of these three commandments, a person could, according to this particular code of ethics, act immorally toward God without acting immorally toward anyone else. The Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:1–17) are listed below:

  • 1. I am the Lord, Your God; do not worship false gods.
  • 2. Do not take the name of God in vain.
  • 3. Keep holy the Sabbath Day.
  • 4. Honor your father and your mother.
  • 5. Do not kill.
  • 6. Do not commit adultery.
  • 7. Do not steal.
  • 8. Do not bear false witness against your neighbor.
  • 9. Do not covet your neighbor’s spouse.
  • 10. Do not covet your neighbor’s belongings.

Notice that commandments one to three are about the relationship with God, while commandments four to ten regulate relationships among human beings. This is why religious morality is distinguished from social morality in the textbook’s framework.

👉 ሃይማኖታዊ ሞራል የሰውን ከአምላክ ጋር ያለውን ግንኙነት ይመለከታል። በአይሁድና በክርስትና ትውፊት የአሥሩ ትእዛዛት የመጀመሪያዎቹ ሶስት ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ያለን ግንኙነት ይመለከታሉ። ለምሳሌ ‘ሌሎችን ሳትጎዳ ብቻ እግዚአብሔርን ብትክድ’ እንኳን፣ በዚህ የሥነ-ምግባር ሕግ መሠረት በእግዚአብሔር ላይ ስህተት ሰርተሃል ማለት ነው። ቀሪዎቹ ሰባቱ (ከአራተኛው እስከ አሥረኛው) ግን የሰዎችን ግንኙነት ይቆጣጠራሉ፤ ለምሳሌ ‘አትግደል’፣ ‘አትስረቅ’ እና ‘ባልንጀራህን አትመስክርበት’ ያሉት ትእዛዛት በማህበራዊ ሞራል ውስጥ ይካተታሉ። በኢትዮጵያ ኦርቶዶክስ ተዋሕዶ ቤተ ክርስቲያን የሚሰጠው ትምህርትና የንስሐ ልምምድ የሃይማኖታዊ ሞራል ምሳሌዎች ናቸው። ✝️

💡 Exam Hint: Religious morality covers the first three commandments (relationship with God). Commandments four to ten belong to social morality. Do not confuse the two groups when a question asks you to classify a commandment.

3.4.2. Morality and Nature

“Morality and nature” refers to a human being in relationship to nature. Natural morality has been prevalent in all primitive cultures, such as that of the Native American, and in cultures of the Far East. More recently, the Western tradition has also become aware of the significance of dealing with nature in a moral manner. Some see nature as being valuable only for the good of humanity, but many others have come to see it as a good in itself, worthy of moral consideration. With this viewpoint there is no question about whether a Robinson Crusoe would be capable of moral or immoral actions on a desert island by himself. In the morality and nature aspect, he could be considered either moral or immoral, depending upon his actions toward the natural things around him.

👉 ሞራልና ተፈጥሮ ሰው ከተፈጥሮ ጋር ያለውን ግንኙነት ይመለከታል። በብዙ ባህላዊ ማህበረሰቦች፣ ለምሳሌ በአሜሪካ ተወላጆችና በምስራቃዊ ባህሎች፣ ተፈጥሮን መጠበቅ ከሥነ-ምግባር ጋር የተያያዘ ነው። አንዳንዶች ተፈጥሮ ለሰው ጥቅም ብቻ ዋጋ አለው ይላሉ፤ ሌሎች ግን በራሱ ዋጋ ያለው ነው ይላሉ። ለምሳሌ በኢትዮጵያ የ‘አረንጓዴ ዐሻራ’ (Green Legacy) የችግኝ ተከላ መርሐ ግብር ተፈጥሮን መንከባከብ የሞራል ኃላፊነት መሆኑን ያሳያል። 🌳

3.4.3. Individual Morality

Individual morality refers to individuals in relation to themselves and to an individual code of morality that may or may not be sanctioned by any society or religion. It allows for a “higher morality,” which can be found within the individual rather than beyond this world in some supernatural realm. A person may or may not perform some particular act, not because society, law, or religion says he may or may not, but because he himself thinks it is right or wrong from within his own conscience.

👉 ግላዊ ሞራል ሰው ከራሱ ጋር ያለውን ግንኙነት የሚመለከት ሲሆን፣ ማህበረሰብም ሆነ ሃይማኖት ያላፀደቀው የራሱ የሥነ-ምግባር ደንብ ሊሆን ይችላል። ሰው አንድን ነገር የሚያደርገው ወይም የማያደርገው ህግ ስለተባለ ሳይሆን፣ በራሱ ህሊና ትክክል ወይም ስህተት ስለሆነ ነው። ለምሳሌ ማንም ሳያይ ከኪሱ የወደቀ ብር ለባለቤቱ የሚመልስ ሰው ግላዊ ሞራል አለው። 🪞

3.4.4. Social Morality

Social morality concerns a human being in relation to other human beings. It is probably the most important aspect of morality, in that it cuts across all of the other aspects and is found in more ethical systems than any of the others. Returning briefly to the desert-island example, most ethicists would probably state that Robinson Crusoe is incapable of any really moral or immoral action except toward himself and nature. Such action would be minimal when compared with the potential for morality or immorality if there were nine other people on the island whom he could subjugate, torture, or destroy. Many ethical systems would allow that what he would do to himself is strictly his business, “as long as it doesn’t harm anyone else.”

👉 ማህበራዊ ሞራል ሰው ከሌሎች ሰዎች ጋር ያለውን ግንኙነት ይመለከታል፤ ከሁሉም የሞራል ገጽታዎች በጣም አስፈላጊው ነው። ሮቢንሰን ክሩሶ በረሃማ ደሴት ላይ ብቻውን ቢሆን ሞራላዊ ድርጊቱ ውስን ይሆናል፤ ሌሎች ዘጠኝ ሰዎች ቢኖሩ ግን ሊያስገድድ፣ ሊያሰቃይ ወይም ሊያጠፋ ይችል ነበር። ስለዚህ ሰዎች በአንድ ማህበረሰብ ውስጥ ሲኖሩ ድርጊታቸው በሌሎች ላይ ተጽእኖ ስለሚያመጣ ሞራላዊ ኃላፊነት ይኖራቸዋል። ‘ሌላውን እስካልጎዳ ድረስ’ የሚለው መርህ ለግል ድርጊት ሲተገበር ይታያል። 🤝

💡 Exam Hint: Social morality is the most important aspect because it cuts across all other aspects. A question about harm or benefit to other people points to social morality, while a question about one’s own conscience points to individual morality.

3.5. Who is Morally/Ethically Responsible?

Morality pertains to human beings and only to human beings; all else is speculation. If one wants to attribute morality to supernatural beings, one has to do so solely on faith. If one wants to hold animals or plants morally responsible for destructive acts against each other or against humans, then one has to ignore most of the evidence that science has given us concerning the instinctual behavior of such beings and the evidence of our own everyday observations. Recent experimentation with the teaching of language to animals suggests that they are at least minimally capable of developing some thought processes similar to those of humans. At the present time, however, most evidence seems to indicate that animals, as well as plants, should be classified as either non-moral or amoral, that is, they should be considered either as having no moral sense or as being out of the moral sphere altogether.

Therefore, when we use the terms moral and ethical, we are using them in reference only to human beings. We do not hold a wolf morally responsible for killing a sheep, or an eagle morally responsible for killing a chicken. We may kill the wolf or fox for having done this act, but we do not kill it because we hold the animal morally responsible. We do it because we don’t want any more of our sheep or chickens to be killed. At this point in the world’s history, only human beings can be moral or immoral, and therefore only human beings should be held morally responsible for their actions and behavior.

👉 ሞራልና ስነ-ምግባር የሚሉት ቃላት የሚያገለግሉት ለሰው ብቻ ነው። ተኩላ በግን ስለገደለ ወይም ንስር ዶሮን ስለገደለ ሞራላዊ ተጠያቂ አናደርገውም። ተኩላውን ወይም ቀበሮውን የምንገድለው በሞራል ምክንያት ሳይሆን ተጨማሪ በጎቻችንና ዶሮዎቻችን እንዳይጠፉ ስለምንፈልግ ነው። ስለዚህ በዚህ ዘመን ሞራላዊ ወይም ኢ-ሞራላዊ መሆን የሚችሉት ሰዎች ብቻ ናቸው፤ ለድርጊታቸውና ባህሪያቸው ተጠያቂ መሆንም ያለባቸው ሰዎች ብቻ ናቸው። ⚖️

💡 Exam Hint: Moral and ethical refer to human beings in this textbook. A wolf can be killed to protect sheep, but the wolf is not morally responsible. Do not confuse harmful with immoral when the agent cannot choose.

3.5.1. Moral Judgments

Moral judgments refer to deciding what is right and what is wrong in human relations. Individuals are continually judging their own conduct and that of their fellows. They approve of some acts and call them “right” or “good”. They condemn other acts and call them “wrong” or “evil or bad”. Moral judgments always have to do with the actions of human beings and, in particular, with voluntary actions, those actions freely chosen. Involuntary actions, those over which people have no control, are rarely open to moral judgment, as a person usually is not held responsible for an action that she or he did not initiate. Moral judgments are evaluative because they place value on things or relations or human actions, determine what is right or wrong, good or bad. They are also normative because they evaluate or assess the moral worth of something based on some norms or standards.

Finding the right course of action, choosing the right alternative, is not always simple. We can have no algorithm for judgment, since every application of a rule would itself need supplementing with further rules. Onora O’Neill argues that moral principles do not provide us with an “auto-pilot for life” and that “judgment is always needed in using or following – and in flouting – rules or principles”. When conflicts of interest arise, the solution may require the greatest sensitivity, experience, discernment, intelligence and goodwill, and even then we may doubt whether we have acted rightly. However, in judging conduct or action we have to consider motives, means, and consequences and sometimes the situation.

👉 ሞራላዊ ፍርድ ማለት በሰዎች ግንኙነት ውስጥ ምን ትክክልና ምን ስህተት እንደሆነ መወሰን ነው። ፍርዶች ግምገማዊ (evaluative) ናቸው፤ ምክንያቱም ለነገሮችና ለድርጊቶች ዋጋ ይሰጣሉ። ደንብ ተኮር (normative) ናቸው፤ ምክንያቱም ድርጊትን በአንድ ደረጃ ወይም ህግ ይለካሉ። በፈቃድ የተደረገ ድርጊት (voluntary) ብቻ ለሞራላዊ ፍርድ ይቀርባል፤ ሰው ያልመረጠውና የማይቆጣጠረው ድርጊት (involuntary) ግን ብዙ ጊዜ አይፈረድበትም። ለምሳሌ ብልሽት ያለው ብሬክ ያለው መኪና ሾፌር አደጋ ቢያደርስ፣ ሆን ብሎ ካላደረገ በቀር ሞራላዊ ፍርድ ላይ ጥፋተኛ ላይሆን ይችላል። ኦኔል ሞራል 'ራስ-በራሪ' (auto-pilot) አይደለም፤ ፍርድ ያስፈልጋል ይላል። ⚖️

3.5.2. What Makes an Action Moral?

Sometimes we think of “moral” as meaning morally good. But philosophically, it refers to an action which comes within the scope of morality, that is, an action which is morally significant either in a positive way (because it is good or right) or in a negative way (because the action is good or bad). Not all actions have a moral sense. Many of the actions we perform in life, such as putting on a raincoat, sharpening a pencil, counting apples, or standing on your head, are not in themselves either good or bad acts. Such actions are morally neutral or non-moral. By contrast, stealing from your library, punching people or helping the disadvantaged are considered as morally significant actions. The following features make an action moral:

  • A. A moral act involves an agent: if something is a natural event or an action performed by animals, then it is morally neutral; it does not appear on our moral radar. Humans can be moral agents, or any creatures that can freely and thoughtfully choose its actions will count as a moral agent.
  • B. A moral act involves intention: an intention here refers to our motives that are important to determine the rightness or wrongness of an action. If an action is done accidentally, it may be counted as a morally neutral action. However, some unintentional acts, such as those done through negligence, can be moral. Neglecting our duties, even accidentally, makes us morally culpable.
  • C. A moral act affects others: a moral action needs not only an agent and to be deliberate but also needs to affect others (those we might call moral patients) in significant ways, that is, an action that has harmful (be it physical, psychological, emotional, or depriving others of happiness) or beneficial consequences for others.

The claim that morality only governs behavior that affects others is somewhat controversial. Some have claimed that morality also governs behavior that affects only the agent herself, such as taking recreational drugs, masturbation, and not developing one’s talents. Confusion about the content of morality arises because morality is not always distinguished from religion. Regarding self-affecting behavior as governed by morality is supported by the idea that we are created by God and are obliged to obey his commands, and so may be a holdover from the time when morality was not clearly distinguished from religion. This religious holdover might also affect the claim that some sexual practices such as homosexuality are immoral; but those who distinguish morality from religion do not regard homosexuality, per se, as a moral matter.

Generally, a moral action is one which is: performed by agents, creatures that are capable of free choice or free will; the result of intention, the action was done on purpose with a particular motive; and has a significant consequence on others in respect of harm or benefits it brings about.

👉 ድርጊት ሞራላዊ የሚሆነው ሶስት ነገሮች ሲኖሩት ነው። (ሀ) ፈጻሚ (agent)፦ በነፃ ፈቃድ የሚመርጥ ፍጡር መሆን አለበት፤ የተፈጥሮ ክስተት ወይም የእንስሳት ድርጊት ሞራላዊ ገለልተኛ ነው። (ለ) ዓላማ (intention)፦ በሆን ተብሎ የተደረገ መሆን አለበት፤ በአጋጣሚ የሆነ ድርጊት ገለልተኛ ቢሆንም፣ በቸልተኝነት የተፈጸመ ድርጊት ግን ሞራላዊ ኃላፊነት ያመጣል። (ሐ) ሌሎችን መነካት (affects others)፦ ጉዳትም ሆነ ጥቅም ለሌሎች ማስከተል አለበት። ለምሳሌ ሰው በገዛ ቤቱ ውስጥ የሚያደርገው ግላዊ ድርጊት ሌሎችን ካልነካ ሞራላዊ ጉዳይ ላይሆን ይችላል። ‘ብቻውን ቢሆን ሞራላዊ ድርጊት የለም’ የሚለው አመለካከት አወዛጋቢ ነው። 🧾

💡 Exam Hint: A moral act needs three features: an agent, an intention and an effect on others. Accidental acts are usually morally neutral, but negligence can still make a person morally culpable. Expect a question on whether a natural event or an animal’s action is moral; it is not, because it has no agent.

Ingredients of Moral Judgment: Motives

Motives, as Jesus, Kant, and others have pointed out, are basic for a determination of morality. The motive refers to the intention or why an action is done. A good motive is a prerequisite to conduct that we approve without qualification. If a good motive is present when an act, through some unforeseen factor, leads to harmful effects, we tend to disapprove less severely and to say, “Anyway, he meant well.” Kant, for example, defined the good as the “good will”: “Nothing can possibly be conceived in the world, or even out of it, which can be called good without qualification, except a good will.” For Kant, a rational being strives to do what he or she ought to do and this is to be distinguished from an act that a person does from either inclination or self-interest. A truly moral act, for Kant, not only agrees with the moral law, but is done for the sake of the moral law, not only as duty requires but because duty requires. In Kantian thinking the seat of moral worth is the individual’s will, and the good will acts out of a sense of duty.

👉 ዓላማ (motive) ሞራላዊ ድርጊትን ለመወሰን መሠረታዊ ነው። ይኸውም ድርጊቱ ለምን እንደተደረገ ነው። ጥሩ ዓላማ ያለው ድርጊት ያለ ምንም ጥያቄ ለመፈቀድ መሠረት ነው። ጥሩ ዓላማ ኖሮ ያልተጠበቀ ጉዳት ቢመጣ ‘ቢሆንም ለበጎ ነበር ያሰበው’ ብለን እንቀንሳለን። ካንት ‘መልካም ፈቃድ’ (good will) ብቻ ያለ ቅድመ ሁኔታ መልካም ነው ይላል። ለምሳሌ ህክምና የሚሰጥ ሃኪም ዝናን ለመፈለግ ሳይሆን ለታካሚው ጤና ብሎ የሚሰጥ ከሆነ ድርጊቱ ከሞራል ግዴታ የመነጨ ነው። ያለ ምንም ፍላጎት ወይም ጥቅም ሲሆን ብቻ ሞራላዊ ዋጋ አለው። 💡

Ingredients of Moral Judgment: Means

Just as there may be many motives for desiring something, there may be many means for achieving it. The term means can be defined as an agency, instrument, or method used to attain an end. Though we expect people to use the best available means to carry out their purposes, we condemn them if their choice of means impresses us as unjust, cruel, or immoral. On rare occasions we may approve of an act when means are used that under other conditions would be condemned. However, there is a danger in proposing that any means may be used, provided the end is good, or that “the end justifies the means.” Once chosen, the means become part of the general effect of an act.

👉 ብዙ ዓላማዎች እንዳሉ ሁሉ ዓላማን ለማሳካት ብዙ መንገዶች (means) ሊኖሩ ይችላሉ። መንገዱ ኢ-ፍትሃዊ፣ ጨካኝ ወይም ኢ-ሞራላዊ ከሆነ ሰውን እንኮንነዋለን። ለምሳሌ ግብር የሚሰበስብ መሥሪያ ቤት ሥራውን በጥሩ ዓላማ ቢሠራም፣ ሰዎችን አስፈራርቶና ደብድቦ ከሆነ መንገዱ ኢ-ሞራላዊ ነው። ‘ግቡ ጥሩ ከሆነ መንገዱ ምንም ቢሆን ይፈቀዳል’ የሚለው አባባል አደገኛ ነው። ⚠️

Ingredients of Moral Judgment: Consequences

Consequences are the effects or results of a moral decision based on a value. We expect the consequences of an act that we call “right” to be good. Ordinarily, when people ask, “what is right?” they are thinking about the consequences of the action. This depends on what ethical principle is in operation. Kant agrees to the good motive, utilitarians to the result. In general, society judges conduct “right” if it proceeds from a good motive, through the use of the best available means, to consequences that are good. If these conditions are not fulfilled, we condemn the action or approve it with reservations. We rarely approve an action when the results are evil or wrong.

👉 መዘዝ (consequences) ማለት የሞራላዊ ውሳኔ ውጤቶችና ተጽእኖዎች ናቸው። ካንት በዓላማ ላይ ሲያተኩር ዩቲሊታሪያኖች ደግሞ በውጤቱ ላይ ያተኩራሉ። በአጠቃላይ ማህበረሰብ ድርጊትን ትክክል የሚለው ጥሩ ዓላማ፣ ተገቢ መንገድና መልካም ውጤት ሲኖሩት ነው። ለምሳሌ ለተቸገረ ጎረቤት ምግብ መስጠት ጥሩ ዓላማ፣ ተገቢ መንገድና መልካም ውጤት ይዞ ትክክል ነው። 🍲

Ingredients of Moral Judgment: The Moral Situation

A moral situation involves moral agents, human beings who act, are empowered to make choices, and consciously make decisions. As moral agents, demands are made on us and place us under obligations: we have both duties and rights. We are faced with moral alternatives, and we can better weigh those alternatives when we have an understanding of the ingredients of the moral situation.

👉 ሞራላዊ ሁኔታ ሞራላዊ ፈጻሚዎችን ያካትታል፤ እነሱም ምርጫ የማድረግና ውሳኔ የመስጠት ኃይል ያላቸው ሰዎች ናቸው። እንደ ሞራላዊ ፈጻሚ ግዴታና መብት አለን። ሞራላዊ አማራጮችን በደንብ ለመመዘን የሁኔታውን ክፍሎች (motives, means, consequences) መረዳት ያስፈልጋል። ለምሳሌ ተማሪ በፈተና ወቅት ‘ጓደኛዬን ልርዳ ወይስ ህጉን ልጠብቅ?’ ብሎ ሲወስን ይህ ሞራላዊ ሁኔታ ነው። 🧩

💡 Exam Hint: Motives explain why an act is done; means explain how; consequences explain what results. A good motive does not automatically justify a harmful means. ‘The end justifies the means’ is a warning, not a rule.

3.6. Why Should Human Beings Be Moral?

The question that is worth mentioning at this point is “Why should human beings be moral?” Another way of putting the problem is as follows: Is there any clear foundation or basis for morality, that is, any reason to be moral, one that does not depend on a supernatural command? There are two distinct components to the question “Why be moral?”: (1) Why does society need moral rules? and (2) Why should I be moral?

From Hobbes’s perspective, morality consists of a set of rules such that, if nearly everyone follows them, then nearly everyone will flourish. These rules restrict our freedom but promote greater freedom and wellbeing. More specifically, the five social benefits of establishing and following moral rules accomplish the following: (a) keep society from falling apart; (b) reduce human suffering; (c) promote human flourishing; (d) resolve conflicts of interest in just and orderly ways; and (e) assign praise and blame, reward and punishment, and guilt.

  • (a) Keep society from falling apart.
  • (b) Reduce human suffering.
  • (c) Promote human flourishing.
  • (d) Resolve conflicts of interest in just and orderly ways.
  • (e) Assign praise and blame, reward and punishment, and guilt.

👉 ለምን ሞራል ያስፈልጋል? ሁለት ጥያቄዎች አሉ፦ (1) ማህበረሰብ ለምን የሞራል ህጎች ያስፈልጉታል? (2) እኔ ለምን ሞራላዊ መሆን አለብኝ? ሆብስ እንደሚለው ሞራል አብዛኛው ሰው ቢከተለው ሁሉም ይበለጽጋል፤ ህጎቹ ነፃነትን ይገድባሉ፤ ነገር ግን የበለጠ ነፃነትና ደህንነት ያመጣሉ። ይህም ማህበረሰብ እንዳይፈርስ፣ ስቃይ እንዲቀንስ፣ ሰዎች እንዲያድጉ፣ የጥቅም ግጭቶች በፍትሃዊ መንገድ እንዲፈቱና ሽልማትና ቅጣት እንዲኖር ያደርጋል። ለምሳሌ በአዲስ አበባ ትራፊክ ህግ ሁሉም ቢከተል አደጋ ይቀንሳል፤ ሰዎችም በደህና ይጓዛሉ። 🚦

💡 Exam Hint: Two questions appear in this section: Why does society need moral rules? and Why should I be moral? Hobbes answers the first with five social benefits. Students often mix up the two; the first is about society, the second about the individual.

The common answers to “Why be moral?” are: behaving morally is a matter of self-respect; people won’t like us if we behave immorally; society punishes immoral behavior; God tells us to be moral; and parents need to be moral role models for their children. These are all good answers, and each may be a powerful motivation for the right person. However, many of these answers won’t apply to every person: nonbelievers, nonparents, people who don’t respect themselves, people who think that they can escape punishment.

👉 ለምን ሞራላዊ መሆን አለብኝ? ለሚለው የተለመዱ መልሶች፦ ሞራል ለራስ ክብር መስጠት ነው፣ ሰዎች ኢ-ሞራላዊ ሲሆኑ አይወዱንም፣ ማህበረሰብ ኢ-ሞራላዊ ባህሪን ይቀጣል፣ እግዚአብሔር ሞራላዊ እንድንሆን ይላል፣ ወላጆች ለልጆቻቸው ምሳሌ መሆን አለባቸው። ነገር ግን እነዚህ መልሶች ለሁሉም ሰው አይሰሩም፤ ለምሳሌ አማኝ ያልሆነ፣ ልጅ የሌለው ወይም ራሱን የማያከብር ሰው ላይ ተጽእኖ ላይኖራቸው ይችላል። 🤔

Let us assume for the moment that there is no supernatural morality and see if we can find any other reasons why people should be moral. One argument is the argument from enlightened self-interest. One can certainly argue that it is, at the very least, generally better to be good rather than bad and to create a world and society that is good rather than one that is bad. As a matter of fact, self-interest is the sole basis of one ethical theory, ethical egoism. However, it is not being suggested at this point that one ought to pursue one’s own self-interest. Rather, an argument is being presented that if everyone tried to be good and tried to avoid and prevent bad, it would be in everyone’s self-interest. For example, if within a group of people no one killed, stole, lied, or cheated, then each member of the group would benefit. An individual member of the group could say, “it’s in my self-interest to do good rather than bad because I stand to benefit if I do and also because I could be ostracized or punished if I don’t.” Therefore, even though it is not airtight, the argument from enlightened self-interest is compelling.

👉 ሰዎች ለምን ጥሩ መሆን አለባቸው? ሌላ ምክንያት 'የበራ ራስ ጥቅም' (enlightened self-interest) ነው። ሁሉም ጥሩ ቢሆን ሁሉም ይጠቀማል፤ መስረቅ፣ መዋሸትና ማጭበርበር ባይኖር ሁሉም በሰላም ይኖራል። ይህ ከኢጎዊ ስነ-ምግባር (ethical egoism) የተለየ ነው፤ ኢጎዊ ስነ-ምግባር ‘ራስህን ብቻ አስብ’ ይላል። ለምሳሌ በኢትዮጵያ ‘ኢድር’ ውስጥ አባላት ለሌላው ይረዳዳሉ፤ ዛሬ የሚረዳ ነገ ሲቸገር ይረዳዋል፤ ይህም የጋራ ራስ ጥቅም ነው። 🤝

💡 Exam Hint: The argument from enlightened self-interest is not the same as ethical egoism. Enlightened self-interest argues that everyone being good serves everyone’s interest; ethical egoism claims that each person ought to pursue only their own interest.

Related to the foregoing argument is the argument from tradition and law. This argument suggests that because traditions and laws, established over a long period of time, govern the behavior of human beings, and because these traditions and laws urge human beings to be moral rather than immoral, there are good reasons for being so. Self-interest is one reason, but another is respect for the human thought and effort that has gone into establishing such laws and traditions and transferring them from one historic period and one culture to another. This can be an attractive argument, even though it tends to suppress questioning of traditions and laws, a kind of questioning that is at the core of creative moral reasoning. It is interesting to note that most of us probably learned morality through being confronted with this argument, the religious argument, and the experiences surrounding it.

👉 ሦስተኛው ምክንያት ትውፊትና ህግ ነው። ለዘመናት የቆዩ ባህሎችና ህጎች ሰዎች ሞራላዊ እንዲሆኑ ያበረታታሉ፤ ይህም ለቀደሙት ሰዎች ጥረት አክብሮት መስጠት ነው። ነገር ግን ትውፊትን መጠየቅ የሞራል ፈጠራ ዋና ክፍል ነው፤ ስለዚህ ትውፊትን ብቻ መከተል ገደብ አለው። ለምሳሌ በኢትዮጵያ ‘ፍትሐ ነገሥት’ እና የአባቶች ሕግጋት ለብዙ ዘመን የማኅበረሰቡን ሥነ-ምግባር ቀርፀዋል፤ ይሁን እንጂ በዘመናዊ ህገ-መንግስትም ሆነ በሰብአዊ መብት እሴቶች መፈተሽ ያስፈልጋል። 📜

Common human needs provide another reason. If we examine human nature as empirically and rationally as we can, we discover that all human beings have many needs, desires, goals, and objectives in common. For example, people generally seem to need friendship, love, happiness, freedom, peace, creativity, and stability in their lives, not only for themselves but for others, too. In order to satisfy these needs, people must establish and follow moral principles that encourage them to cooperate with one another and that free them from fear that they will lose their lives, be mutilated, or be stolen from, lied to, cheated, severely restricted, or imprisoned. As John Hospers puts it: “Morality is not of course identical with following self-interest. If it were, there could be no conflict between morality and self-interest and no point in having rules overriding self-interest.”

Morality exists, in part, because of human needs and through recognition of the importance of living together in a cooperative and significant way. It may not be the case that all human beings can be convinced that they should be moral, or even that it will always be in each individual’s self-interest to be moral. However, the question “why should human beings be moral?” generally can best be answered by the statement that adhering to moral principles enables human beings to live their lives as peacefully, happily, creatively, and meaningfully as is possible.

👉 ሦስተኛው ምክንያት የሰዎች የጋራ ፍላጎት ነው። ሁሉም ሰው ጓደኝነት፣ ፍቅር፣ ደስታ፣ ነፃነት፣ ሰላምና መረጋጋት ይፈልጋል። እነዚህን ለማግኘት ሰዎች በጋራ እንዲተባበሩና ከፍርሃት እንዲላቀቁ የሚያደርጉ የሞራል መርሆች ያስፈልጋሉ። ሆስፐርስ እንደሚለው ሞራል ከራስ ጥቅም ጋር ፈጽሞ አንድ አይደለም። ሞራል ሰው ሰላማዊ፣ ደስተኛ፣ ፈጠራ ያለው እና ትርጉም ያለው ሕይወት እንዲኖር ያስችላል፤ ስለዚህ ‘ለምን ሞራላዊ መሆን አለብን?’ ለሚለው ዋናው መልስ ይኸው ነው። ❤️
